q: Does it matter for CBAM if an extruder uses primary or secondary aluminium billet?
title: Extruders: primary vs secondary billet
short: Yes. For aluminium products, unwrought aluminium is the precursor, and the Commission's guidance says to tell primary from secondary where known. Primary comes from electrolytic smelting, secondary from remelting scrap, and their embedded emissions differ, so the billet mix shapes your profile's figure.
audience: Indian aluminium extruders and profile makers exporting under CN 7604, 7608 and 7610

ul: Embedded emissions of the billet you consume, split by primary and secondary where known.
Your own direct emissions from homogenising, extrusion and other heating.
Electricity is not counted for aluminium goods.
Billet purchases by supplier and type, in tonnes, for the calendar year.
Each billet supplier's verified figure, or a note that you will use default values.
Your output in tonnes, by CN code.

p: Scrap itself is not a precursor and carries no upstream emissions, which is why secondary billet tends to come out lower.
